facts.statement: Savannasaurus lived during the Cenomanian to Lower Turonian stages of the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Cenomanian–Lower Turonian, ~

facts.statement: Savannasaurus fossils were found in the Late Cretaceous Winton Formation of Queensland, Australia.
facts.quote: Savannasaurus is a genus of titanosaurian sauropod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous Winton Formation of Queensland, Australia.

facts.statement: The species Savannasaurus elliottorum was named in 2016 by Stephen Poropat and colleagues.
facts.quote: It contains one species, Savannasaurus elliottorum, named in 2016 by Stephen Poropat and colleagues.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen, nicknamed "Wade", is the most complete Australian sauropod known and is held at the Australian Age of Dinosaurs museum.
facts.quote: The holotype and only known specimen, originally nicknamed "Wade", is the most complete specimen of an Australian sauropod, and is held at the Australian Age of Dinosaurs museum.

facts.statement: The first Savannasaurus specimen was discovered in March 2005 by David Elliot and his family.
facts.quote: In March 2005, the first specimen of Savannasaurus was discovered by David Elliot, founder of Australian Age of Dinosaurs (AODF), along with his wife Judy and their children.

facts.statement: The specimen was preserved in a siltstone concretion that was split using jackhammers and chisels to allow for reassembly.
facts.quote: A siltstone concretion containing the specimen was split along gypsum-filled fractures using jackhammers and chisels, with the pieces being marked to facilitate reassembly.

facts.statement: Preparing the specimen took approximately ten years using air scribes and micro-jacks.
facts.quote: Preparation of the specimen took around a decade, with air scribes and micro-jacks being used.

facts.statement: Specimen AODF 660 consists of approximately 40 bones.
facts.quote: AODF 660 consists of around 40 bones

facts.statement: This specimen represents about 20% to 25% of the animal and is the most complete sauropod known from Australia.
facts.quote: The specimen is the most complete sauropod specimen known from Australia, and represents approximately 20% to 25% of the animal.

facts.statement: The specimen was formally described and named in 2016 by Stephen Poropat and colleagues.
facts.quote: Having been nicknamed "Wade", AODF 660 was formally described and named in 2016 by Stephen Poropat and colleagues in a paper that also described a skull belonging to Diamantinasaurus.

facts.statement: The generic name refers to the savanna environment, and the specific name honors the Elliott family.
facts.quote: the generic name of Savannasaurus, from Taíno zavana (the root of the word "savanna"), refers to the environment in which it was found, while the specific name elliottorum honours the Elliott family and their contributions to Australian palaeontology.

facts.statement: Savannasaurus was a medium-sized titanosaur measuring 15 meters in length.
facts.quote: At 15 m long, Savannasaurus was a medium-sized titanosaur.

facts.statement: Savannasaurus had wide hips that were over 1.1 meters wide at their widest points.
facts.quote: It is notable for its wide hips, which would have been over 1.1 m wide at their widest points.

facts.statement: Traits like wide hips and a flexible spine likely helped Savannasaurus navigate muddy floodplains.
facts.quote: Combined with a flexible vertebral column, these traits would have made Savannasaurus better at navigating the muddy ground of the floodplains that it lived on.

facts.statement: Savannasaurus is considered an early-diverging member of the Titanosauria but not part of the specialized group Lithostrotia.
facts.quote: Various traits suggest that Savannasaurus was an early-diverging (or basal) member of the Titanosauria, but not a member of the more specialized group Lithostrotia.

facts.statement: Analyses suggest Savannasaurus ancestors migrated to Australia through Antarctica around 105 to 100 million years ago.
facts.quote: Palaeobiogeographic analyses suggest that the ancestors of Savannasaurus and Diamantinasaurus were from either Asia or one of the southern Gondwanan continents; regardless, they likely migrated to Australia through Antarctica around 105–100 million years ago.

facts.statement: Associated teeth suggest that the theropod Australovenator may have fed on the Savannasaurus holotype.
facts.quote: associated teeth suggest that Australovenator may have fed on the holotype specimen.

facts.statement: Savannasaurus measured about 15 meters long, weighed around 20 tons, and had a shoulder height of approximately 3 meters.
facts.quote: Savannasaurus was a medium-sized titanosaur that measured about 15 m in length, with a weight of around 20 t and a shoulder height of around 3 m.

facts.statement: Poropat and colleagues suggested the undulating front articulating surface of one caudal centrum as a distinguishing characteristic of Savannasaurus.
facts.quote: Poropat and colleagues suggested this as a distinguishing characteristic of Savannasaurus

facts.statement: The other caudal vertebrae of Savannasaurus were amphicoelous, having centra concave on both ends, a trait rare among titanosaurs except in Baotianmansaurus and Dongyangosaurus.
facts.quote: The other caudals were amphicoelous, or having centra that are concave on both ends, which was also rare among titanosaurs save for Baotianmansaurus and Dongyangosaurus

facts.statement: The known cervical vertebra of Savannasaurus had a well-developed longitudinal fossa extending for nearly its entire length.
facts.quote: There was a well-developed longitudinal fossa, or excavation, along the side of the vertebra that extends for nearly its entire length

facts.statement: The laminae in the dorsal vertebrae of Savannasaurus were bilaterally asymmetric, with the left side being better reinforced by extra laminae.
facts.quote: Notably, the laminae in the dorsals of Savannasaurus were bilaterally asymmetric; the left side of the vertebrae would have been better reinforced by extra laminae

facts.statement: The sternal plates of Savannasaurus lacked the long ridges present on the bottom surfaces of most Neosauropoda.
facts.quote: Second, they lacked the long ridges that were present on the bottom surfaces among most members of Neosauropoda

facts.statement: In Savannasaurus, the sternal plates were approximately 71% as long as the humeri.
facts.quote: the sternal plates would have been at least 65% as long as the humeri (in Savannasaurus, the ratio was approximately 71%)

facts.statement: The glenoid fossa on the coracoid of Savannasaurus was much larger than that of Diamantinasaurus.
facts.quote: the glenoid fossa on it (which articulated with the humerus) was much larger than that of Diamantinasaurus

facts.statement: The third metacarpal of Savannasaurus was 49% the length of the radius, which is short for a titanosaur but meets the minimum of 45% found in all macronarians.
facts.quote: The third metacarpal was 49% the length of the radius, which was short for a titanosaur, but was at least 45% as in all macronarians

facts.statement: The presence of phalanges in the hands of Savannasaurus is unusual, as all other titanosaurs except Diamantinasaurus had hands formed only by metacarpals.
facts.quote: The presence of phalanges is unusual; all titanosaurs but Savannasaurus and Diamantinasaurus had hands formed only by metacarpals

facts.statement: In Savannasaurus, the ischium's articulation on the pubis was 56% as high as the bone was long, which is higher than in most titanosaurs.
facts.quote: The ischium's articulation on the pubis was 56% as high as the bone was long, higher than most titanosaurs

facts.statement: On the ischium of Savannasaurus, the iliac peduncle was only 32% of the bone's length, which is lower than in most other sauropods.
facts.quote: On the ischium, the iliac peduncle, one of the processes surrounding the acetabulum (hip joint), was only 32% of the bone's length, lower than most other sauropods

facts.statement: Researchers noted the possibility that hyposphene-hypantrum articulations, which argue against a basal position, could have evolved independently multiple times among titanosaurs.
facts.quote: However, Poropat and colleagues recognized the possibility that they could have been acquired independently multiple times among titanosaurs.

facts.statement: A 2017 analysis by Royo-Torres et al. placed Savannasaurus and Diamantinasaurus as successively basal to a clade containing Baotianmansaurus and Dongyanosaurus.
facts.quote: Royo-Torres and colleagues repeated their 2017 analysis after removing a titanosauriform from the Cloverly Formation, Chubutisaurus, and Angolatitan; they found instead that Savannasaurus and Diamantinasaurus were successively basal to a clade consisting of Baotianmansaurus and Dongyanosaurus.

facts.statement: Mannion et al. found Savannasaurus within Saltasauridae in 2019 when using equal weighting, but this result disappeared when using implied weighting.
facts.quote: In their 2019 redescription of Jiangshanosaurus and Dongyanosaurus, Mannion and colleagues found both Savannasaurus and Diamantinasaurus inside Saltasauridae by equally weighting characteristics in their dataset, but using implied weighting eliminated this result.

facts.statement: Palaeobiogeographic analysis suggests the ancestors of Savannasaurus were likely Asian.
facts.quote: Using the modern geography of the continents, they found that the ancestors of the Australian sauropods Savannasaurus, Diamantinasaurus, and Wintonotitan were likely Asian.

facts.statement: Models incorporating Cretaceous geography suggest Savannasaurus ancestors had ranges spanning South America, Africa, and Indo-Madagascar.
facts.quote: Incorporating Cretaceous geography suggested ancestral ranges also spanning the Gondwanan continents of South America, Africa, and Indo-Madagascar.

facts.statement: During the Aptian to early Albian epochs, the region of Australia where Savannasaurus later lived was at 70°S latitude with a cool, temperate climate.
facts.quote: In the Aptian to early Albian epochs, this region of Australia would have been situated at a latitude of 70°S, with a cool, temperate climate.

facts.statement: The only known specimen of Savannasaurus was originally nicknamed "Wade".

facts.statement: Savannasaurus lived during the Late Cretaceous, approximately 94 million years ago in the Turonian stage.

facts.statement: The rock unit containing Savannasaurus fossils, the upper Winton Formation, is dated to about 93.9 million years ago at the Cenomanian-Turonian boundary.
facts.quote: The Belmont sheep station is part of the fossil-bearing rock units in the upper Winton Formation, which has been dated to around or just after the boundary between the Cenomanian and Turonian epochs of the Cretaceous—about 93.9 million years ago

facts.statement: During the Cenomanian and Turonian, the area where Savannasaurus lived was located at a latitude of approximately 50°S.
facts.quote: During the Cenomanian and Turonian, the Winton area had a latitude of around 50°S.

facts.statement: The growing season in the habitat of Savannasaurus would have lasted eight to nine months.
facts.quote: The growing season would have been eight to nine months long.

facts.statement: Researchers suggested the unusual form of the astragalus was an adaptation for weight-bearing, but noted this was unclear due to the absence of other hindlimb bones.
facts.quote: They also suggested that the unusual form of the astragalus was also an adaptation to weight-bearing, but the absence of other hindlimb bones made this unclear.

facts.statement: Poropat and colleagues noted traits that increased vertebral column flexibility, including the absence of hyposphene-hypantrum articulations and prominent excavations below the transprezygapophyseal laminae.
facts.quote: Yet, Poropat and colleagues also noted traits that would have increased the flexibility of the vertebral column, namely the absence of hyposphene-hypantrum articulations and the presence of prominent excavations (the centroprezygapophyseal fossae) below the transprezygapophyseal laminae.

facts.statement: Geological evidence suggests Savannasaurus lived on a freshwater floodplain with broad, meandering river channels subject to occasional flooding.
facts.quote: These rocks suggest that Savannasaurus lived on a freshwater floodplain covered in broad, meandering river channels with low-energy waterflow, which was subject to occasional flooding.

facts.statement: A tooth of Australovenator found near the Savannasaurus holotype suggests the theropod's feeding caused the specimen's disarticulation.
facts.quote: A tooth belonging to Australovenator was found near the Savannasaurus holotype, suggesting that its feeding was responsible for the specimen's disarticulation.

facts.statement: Savannasaurus was a medium-sized titanosaur approximately 15 meters long.
facts.quote: Con 15 metros de largo, Savannasaurus era un titanosauriano de tamaño mediano.

facts.statement: Savannasaurus is notable for its wide hips, which would have been over 1.1 meters wide at their widest points.
facts.quote: Es notable por sus anchas caderas, que habrían tenido más de 1,1 metros de ancho en sus puntos más anchos.

facts.statement: Combined with a flexible spine, Savannasaurus's wide hips and robust limbs would have helped it navigate the muddy floodplains where it lived.
facts.quote: Combinados con una columna vertebral flexible, estos rasgos habrían hecho que Savannasaurus navegara mejor por el suelo fangoso de las llanuras aluviales en las que vivía.

facts.statement: Savannasaurus is classified within the unranked family Titanosauria.
facts.quote: unranked_familia: Titanosauria

facts.statement: Various traits suggest Savannasaurus was an early-diverging or basal member of Titanosauria, but not a member of the specialized group Lithostrotia.
facts.quote: Varios rasgos sugieren que Savannasaurus era un miembro de Titanosauria que divergió temprano o basal, pero no un miembro del grupo más especializado Lithostrotia.

facts.statement: Paleobiogeographic analyses suggest the ancestors of Savannasaurus and Diamantinasaurus likely migrated from Asia or southern Gondwana to Australia via Antarctica between 105 and 100 million years ago.
facts.quote: Los análisis paleobiogeográficos sugieren que los antepasados de Savannasaurus y Diamantinasaurus eran de Asia o de uno de los continentes del sur de Gondwana que probablemente emigraron a Australia a través de la Antártida hace entre 105 y 100 millones de años.

facts.statement: Savannasaurus was a medium-sized titanosaur reaching approximately 15 meters in length.
facts.quote: Savannasaurus es un titanosaurio de tamaño mediano, con cerca de 15 metros de longitud.

facts.statement: Savannasaurus had an unusually wide body, with its fused sacrum and ischium-pubis structure being nearly one meter wide at its narrowest points.
facts.quote: El sacro y la estructura fusionada del isquion y el pubis tienen cerca de un metro de ancho en sus puntos más estrechos, lo que hace a Savannasaurus un titanosauriano con un cuerpo inusualmente ancho.

facts.statement: Researchers identified that the first tail vertebrae of Savannasaurus had shallow holes or pits on their sides, a trait previously known only in brachiosaurids.
facts.quote: los descriptores identificaron varias otras características distintivas: las primeras vértebras caudales tienen agujeros poco profundos, o fosas en sus costados, un rasgo que antes solo era conocido en los braquiosáuridos.

facts.statement: The sternum plates of Savannasaurus had straight edges rather than kidney shapes, and the fourth metacarpal ended in an hourglass shape.
facts.quote: Los bordes de las placas del esternón son rectas, no en forma de riñón como en otros titanosaurianos; el extremo del cuarto metacarpiano tiene forma de reloj de arena.

facts.statement: Savannasaurus possessed a crest on one side of the pubis extending forward and downward from the obturator foramen, and its astragalus was longer than it was wide or high.
facts.quote: Hay una cresta en un lado del pubis extendiéndose hacia adelante y hacia abajo desde el foramen obturador y la longitud del astrágalo es mayor que su ancho o alto.

facts.statement: Like other titanosauriforms, the internal structure of Savannasaurus vertebrae was pneumatized and filled with air due to small holes or chambers, and the dorsal ribs also possessed pneumatic cavities.
facts.quote: Como ocurre en otros titanosauriformes, la estructura interna de las vértebras está neumatizada, llena de aire, gracias a varios pequeños agujeros o cámaras, y las costillas dorsales también poseen cavidades neumáticas.

facts.statement: Savannasaurus dorsal vertebrae had side crests on their underside like Diamantinasaurus and Opisthocoelicaudia but lacked the keel found in those genera, and its dorsal neural spines did not split, unlike Opisthocoelicaudia.
facts.quote: Las vértebras dorsales tienen crestas a los lados en su cara inferior como en Diamantinasaurus y Opisthocoelicaudia, pero Savannasaurus carece de la quilla en la cara inferior de estas vértebras que si se observa en esos géneros; las espinas neurales dorsales además no se bifurcan, a diferencia de Opisthocoelicaudia.

facts.statement: Known cervical and dorsal vertebrae of Savannasaurus were opisthocoelous, while all known tail vertebrae were amphicoelous, differing from most titanosaurians.
facts.quote: Las vértebras cervicales y dorsales conocidas son opistocelas, mientras que todas las vértebras caudales son anficelosas, a diferencia de la mayoría de los titanosaurios.

facts.statement: Like most other Titanosauriforms, Savannasaurus vertebrae were pneumatized by small holes created by air sacs and lacked hypospheno-hipantrous articulations that allowed neighboring vertebrae to interlock.
facts.quote: Al igual que con la mayoría de los otros miembros de los Titanosauriformes, las vértebras de Savannasaurus eran neumatizadas por pequeños agujeros creados por sacos de aire, y carecían de articulaciones hiposfeno-hipántro que permitieran entrelazarse las vértebras vecinas.

facts.statement: Poropat and colleagues suggested that the undulating front articular surface of one caudal centrum, concave on the top half and convex on the bottom, was a distinctive feature of Savannasaurus.
facts.quote: Inusualmente, la superficie de articulación frontal de uno de los centros caudales era ondulada, siendo cóncava en la mitad superior y convexa en la mitad inferior. Poropat y sus colegas sugirieron esto como una característica distintiva de Savannasaurus.

facts.statement: The other tail vertebrae of Savannasaurus were amphicoelous with concave centers at both ends, a rarity among titanosaurians except in Baotianmansaurus and Dongyangosaurus.
facts.quote: Los otros caudales eran anfícoelicos, tenían centros cóncavos en ambos extremos, lo que también era raro entre los titanosaurianos a excepción de Baotianmansaurus y Dongyangosaurus.

facts.statement: Unlike most titanosaurians but similar to the ancestral condition among sauropods, the known cervical vertebra of Savannasaurus had a subtle keel running longitudinally along its underside, a trait also found in Mendozasaurus, Overosaurus, Austroposeidon, and Rapetosaurus.
facts.quote: A diferencia de la mayoría de los titanosaurianos, pero similar a la condición "ancestral", plesiomórfica, entre los saurópodos, la vértebra tenía una quilla sutil que corría longitudinalmente a lo largo de su superficie inferior, tanto Mendozasaurus, Overosaurus, Austroposeidon y Rapetosaurus también tienen tales quillas.

facts.statement: The known cervical vertebra of Savannasaurus had a well-developed longitudinal fossa or excavation extending almost its entire length, unlike many titanosaurians where it was weak or absent.
facts.quote: Había una fosa longitudinal bien desarrollada , o excavación, a lo largo del lado de la vértebra que se extiende por casi toda su longitud, a diferencia de muchos titanosaurianos donde era débil o ausente por completo.

facts.statement: Unlike specialized titanosaurians like Saltasauridae, the parapophysis in Savannasaurus was restricted to the front half of the centrum.
facts.quote: En contraste con los titanosaurianos más especializados como los Saltasauridae, la parapófisis, una de las articulaciones de las costillas, estaba restringida a la mitad frontal del centro.

facts.statement: Like most other Somphospondyli members, the sides of the Savannasaurus centrum had teardrop-shaped pneumatic foramina.
facts.quote: Como la mayoría de los otros miembros del Somphospondyli, los lados del centro tienen orificios neumáticos en forma de lágrima.

facts.statement: The dorsal vertebrae of Savannasaurus had bilaterally asymmetric laminae, with the left side likely reinforced by additional laminae.
facts.quote: En particular, las láminas de las dorsales de Savannasaurus eran asimétricas bilateralmente, el lado izquierdo de las vértebras se habría reforzado mejor con láminas adicionales.

facts.statement: Unlike Opisthocoelicaudia, the dorsal neural spines of Savannasaurus increased in height toward the posterior dorsals, did not split into two, and were taller than their corresponding articular surfaces.
facts.quote: También a diferencia de Opisthocoelicaudia, las espinas neurales dorsales en la parte superior del centro aumentaron en altura hacia las dorsales posteriores, no se dividieron en dos y eran más altas que sus superficies articulares correspondientes.

facts.statement: Like the non-titanosaurian somphospondyl Padillasaurus, the front caudal centrum of Savannasaurus had shallow pneumatic excavations on the sides surrounding small holes, whereas most Somphospondyli members have only the holes without excavations.
facts.quote: Al igual que el somfospondilo Padillasaurus, que no es titanosauriano, el centro caudal delantero tenía excavaciones neumáticas poco profundas en los lados que rodeaban pequeños agujeros, mientras que la mayoría de los miembros del Somphospondyli solo tienen los agujeros y no las excavaciones.

facts.statement: The centra of caudals B, C, and D had approximately the same length, suggesting that centrum length did not vary considerably in Savannasaurus.
facts.quote: Los centros de los caudales "B", "C" y "D" tenían aproximadamente la misma longitud, lo que sugiere que la longitud del centro no varió considerablemente.

facts.quote: Parent group: Diamantinasauria

facts.quote: Class: Saurischia
